items.title: Al Rose Interview, 1976-02-24
items.q: I have certainly never questioned that [Biggs was a highly competent artist]... I felt that I understood him well enough to know where he would go.

ctx.x: They probably do. But my point would be that it's been translated in some other way. Oh, very possible. Now, it may, I don't know what a modern analogy to that would be, but I think that all romanticism is taken out. For instance, sexual connotations in those movies were very, it was the dreamy, elusive, very suggestive, subtly suggestive sexuality. No overt sexuality at all. Very subtly suggestive. Oh, of course. Now, today you get the exact opposite. That's true. If there's any less subtle suggestiveness of sex…

Well, there's no question that Biggs was a highly competent artist. I have certainly never questioned that. The fact is that all I have said is that he does not have the emotional appeal for me because I really don't identify with his attitudes. But I certainly can't understand why many people will respond to what he's doing on a basis other than nostalgic.

Well, does he really have the, does he really, does his music really reflect those, those attitudes of that kind of image that you just described? Or is that something you may be reading into his music? Or that other people are doing?
